In article <Sep21.230930.11652@acs.ucalgary.ca>,
Wayne Pearson <wpearson@acs.ucalgary.ca> wrote:
>
>  I must be missing something here, but our group isn't sure what "being in
>torpor" means.  When a vampire oges into torpor (from non-aggravated damage,
>say,) during battle, can that battle be pressed by the other vampire, to do
>even more damage (or kill the torpored vampire)?  Or, does combat end 
>IMMEDIATELY when a vampire goes into torpor? 

When a vampire goes into torpor during combat, whether from normal or 
aggravated damage, combat ends.  You can't press and keep pounding the 
torpid vampire (even if you've played Trap or something) cause he's just 
'gone.'  I'm also pretty sure that no 'additional strikes' can be played 
once a vampire goes into torpor (someone on the 'net, correct me if I'm 
wrong..).  So, play your strikes so that you do max damage _as_ you send 
your opponent into torpor cause you won't get another chance during that 
combat to hurt 'em more!

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Wayne Pearson <wpearson@acs.ucalgary.ca> wrote:
>  I must be missing something here, but our group isn't sure what "being in
>torpor" means.  When a vampire oges into torpor (from non-aggravated damage,
>say,) during battle, can that battle be pressed by the other vampire, to do
>even more damage (or kill the torpored vampire)?  Or, does combat end 
>IMMEDIATELY when a vampire goes into torpor? 

Torpor is a section of the playing area where vampires go to heal; their
actions are very limited while there, as are their interactions with the
rest of the game.  When a vampire goes to torpor during combat, the combat
ends immediately, just as if a strike: combat ends had been played.
